arrival.spacebreaker.ariel: The youngest face among Uranus' moons: long, flat-floored valleys where icy lava once flowed.
arrival.spacebreaker.bennu: A loose rubble pile darker than coal. Nothing here is solid rock: tread lightly.
arrival.spacebreaker.callisto: The most cratered surface known, unchanged for four billion years. Bright frost caps every crater rim.
arrival.spacebreaker.ceres: The largest body in the asteroid belt. Bright salt spots mark where brine reached the surface; ice lies underneath.
arrival.spacebreaker.charon: Pluto's twin: the two always show each other the same face, so Pluto never moves in this sky.
arrival.spacebreaker.churyumov_gerasimen: A two-lobed comet nucleus under dust darker than charcoal. In sunlight, jets of gas lift from the ice.
arrival.spacebreaker.enceladus: Fountains of ice spray from the cracks at the south pole, feeding Saturn's E ring.
arrival.spacebreaker.encke: The comet with the shortest orbit, back near the Sun every 3.3 years: old, small and nearly worn out.
arrival.spacebreaker.eros: A long stony asteroid, the first ever orbited and landed on by a spacecraft.
arrival.spacebreaker.europa: A smooth shell of ice over a hidden ocean. The reddish cracks are where the ocean touched the surface.
arrival.spacebreaker.ganymede: The largest moon in the solar system: old dark plains crossed by bright, grooved ice.
arrival.spacebreaker.halley: The most famous comet, seen from Earth for over two thousand years: a long nucleus blacker than coal.
arrival.spacebreaker.hydra: The brightest ground in Pluto's system: almost pure water ice.
arrival.spacebreaker.io: The most volcanic world known. Sulfur lakes and lava stay hot here: watch where you step.
arrival.spacebreaker.itokawa: A peanut of two rubble lumps; the smooth gravel of the Muses Sea lies in its neck.
arrival.spacebreaker.miranda: A patchwork moon with the tallest cliff known. In this gravity a fall from the top lasts minutes.
arrival.spacebreaker.nereid: On the most stretched orbit of any moon: Neptune shrinks to a small blue disc out here.
arrival.spacebreaker.nix: A tumbling shard of water ice. A strong jump here could almost reach orbit.
arrival.spacebreaker.oberon: Old, cratered ice with dark-floored craters and a mountain about 11 km high.
arrival.spacebreaker.pluto: A heart-shaped plain of nitrogen ice, slowly churning, under a thin blue haze.
arrival.spacebreaker.proteus: Too small to pull itself round, and darker than soot. The Pharos basin nearly broke it apart.
arrival.spacebreaker.ryugu: A spinning top of carbon-rich rubble, with a ridge round its waist.
arrival.spacebreaker.titan: A thick orange sky and lakes of liquid methane. The air is dense enough to fly through, and freezing.
arrival.spacebreaker.titania: Uranus' largest moon, split by canyons hundreds of kilometres long.
arrival.spacebreaker.triton: The coldest surface ever measured. Nitrogen geysers on the southern cap throw dark plumes kilometres high.
arrival.spacebreaker.umbriel: The darkest of Uranus' large moons, except for the bright ring on the floor of Wunda crater.
arrival.spacebreaker.vesta: A battered protoplanet. Its south pole is one vast impact basin with a mountain three times the height of Everest.

gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about.callisto: An old, cratered moon of ice and rock, outside Jupiter's worst radiation.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about.ceres: The largest body in the asteroid belt, with bright salt patches in its craters.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about.charon: Pluto's big moon: the two circle each other like a pair.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about.deimos: Mars's tiny outer moon: you could almost jump off it.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about.earth: Home: air to breathe, water and a blue sky.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about.enceladu: A bright little ice moon that sprays water into space.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about.europa: An ice shell over a hidden ocean, deep in Jupiter's radiation.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about.ganymede: The largest moon in the Solar System, bigger than Mercury.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about.io: Jupiter's volcanic moon: sulphur plains and fountains of lava.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about.jupiter: The biggest planet, a storm-striped ball of gas. Its radiation belts are deadly.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about.mars: The red planet: thin cold air, giant canyons and ice at the poles. Its ice can be made into rocket fuel.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about.mercury: The smallest planet, closest to the Sun: scorching by day, freezing by night.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about.miranda: A small moon of Uranus with cliffs taller than any on Earth.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about.moon: Earth's grey companion: no air, low gravity, dusty seas of old lava.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about.neptune: The farthest planet: deep blue, cold and windy.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about.phobos: Mars's larger moon, a lumpy rock that skims low over the planet.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about.pluto: A small icy world at the edge of the planets, with a heart-shaped plain.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about.saturn: The ringed giant: a world of gas lighter than water.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about.titan: A moon with thick orange haze and lakes of liquid methane.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about.triton: Neptune's frozen moon, with geysers of nitrogen.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about.uranus: A pale blue ice giant that rolls around the Sun on its side.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about.venus: Earth's twin in size, hidden under acid clouds. The air on the ground would crush a submarine.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about.vesta: A battered asteroid with a mountain twice as tall as Everest.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about_kind.ast: A lump of rock left over from the birth of the planets.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about_kind.com: A dirty snowball on a long, stretched orbit: near the Sun its ice boils off into a glowing tail.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about_kind.dwa: A small world, too light to clear its own path around the Sun.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about_kind.gas: A giant ball of gas with no ground to stand on.
gui.spacebreaker.star_map.about_kind.ice: A cold giant of gas and ice, with no ground to stand on.

recipe_viewer.spacebreaker.info.atmosphe: Compresses the local atmosphere and separates its most useful gas: carbon dioxide on Mars and Venus, oxygen from Earth's air, methane on Titan. Output grows with the gas share and the air pressure; it does nothing in vacuum. Needs power.
recipe_viewer.spacebreaker.info.rocket_a: Rockets are not crafted. Place parts (engines, tanks, capsule, fins, parachutes...) in the Rocket Assembler, check the design's delta-v and thrust-to-weight on its screen, then assemble the rocket onto a launch pad. Parts come from the Fabricator; better parts need research.
sensor.spacebreaker.title: Environment reading
subtitles.spacebreaker.mission_control.e: Mission control: Entry interface, expect blackout
tech.spacebreaker.acid_resistant_coating: Fluoropolymer skins and gold-plated contacts that survive the sulfuric-acid clouds of Venus.
tech.spacebreaker.advanced_electronics.d: Radiation-hardened processors and silicon wafers grown in clean rooms.
tech.spacebreaker.aerial_mobility.desc: On Titan the air is four times denser than Earth's and gravity a seventh: a small rotorcraft can hop between dunes and lakes on a battery.
tech.spacebreaker.airlocks.desc: Two doors and a pump: step outside without letting the whole base breathe out.
tech.spacebreaker.aluminium_smelting.des: Refine bauxite into alumina and reduce it to the light metal every rocket is made of.
tech.spacebreaker.asteroid_mining.desc: Nickel-iron and platinum-group metals, waiting in the belt between Mars and Jupiter.
tech.spacebreaker.astrobiology.desc: Where could life survive out there, and how would we recognise it?
tech.spacebreaker.basic_rocketry.desc: Action and reaction: why a rocket flies, and how thrust, mass and burn time fit together.
tech.spacebreaker.brine_chemistry.desc: Salts left behind by drying brines (sodium carbonate, ammonium chloride) are feedstock for soils, glass and coolants far from Earth.
tech.spacebreaker.cloud_platforms.desc: Breathable air is a lifting gas on Venus: float a base 50 km above the furnace.
tech.spacebreaker.cryobot_drilling.desc: A heated probe that melts its way down through kilometres of ice, paying out a tether behind it: the way into Europa's hidden ocean.
tech.spacebreaker.cryogenics.desc: Liquefy oxygen at −183 °C and hydrogen at −253 °C, and store them without boil-off.
tech.spacebreaker.cryovolcanism.desc: Sunlight warms the nitrogen under Triton's clear polar ice until it bursts out in geysers kilometres high: a volcano that runs on frost.
tech.spacebreaker.deep_space_habitats.de: Buried, pressurised modules with their own power and air, built far from help: Callisto, outside Jupiter's worst radiation, is the place to start.
tech.spacebreaker.deep_space_network.des: Giant dishes that can hear a probe's faint signal from beyond Saturn.
tech.spacebreaker.dust_proof_seals.desc: Martian dust is finer than flour and full of salts: labyrinth seals and electrostatic wipers keep joints, airlocks and bearings working.
tech.spacebreaker.electrolysis.desc: Split water into hydrogen and oxygen with electricity.
tech.spacebreaker.electronics.desc: Circuit boards, motors and sensors: the nervous system of every machine.
tech.spacebreaker.eva_mobility.desc: A backpack manoeuvring unit: cold-gas thrusters for moving freely in zero gravity.
tech.spacebreaker.field_geology.desc: Read rocks like a book: collect, label and analyse samples from every world.
tech.spacebreaker.fuel_refining.desc: Pump crude oil and distil it into RP-1 rocket kerosene and plastics.
tech.spacebreaker.fusion_drive.desc: Magnetically confined fusion exhaust: the road to the outer planets in weeks, not years.
tech.spacebreaker.fusion_power.desc: Helium-3 and deuterium in a magnetic bottle: the power source of the stars.
tech.spacebreaker.gravity_assists.desc: Steal a little of a planet's orbital speed by flying close behind it.
tech.spacebreaker.guidance_systems.desc: Gyroscopes, a flight computer and small thrusters to hold attitude and fly a gravity turn.
tech.spacebreaker.heat_resistant_electro: Silicon carbide chips and ceramic boards that keep thinking at 460 °C, on Venus' surface or Mercury's day side.
tech.spacebreaker.heated_suits.desc: Thick foam insulation and battery heaters for Titan's freezing nitrogen air.
tech.spacebreaker.heavy_launch.desc: Reinforced pads and bigger towers for super-heavy, three-stage rockets.
tech.spacebreaker.hydrocarbon_processing: Methane and ethane straight from the lakes, tholins from the dunes: fuel and plastics lying on the ground, waiting for oxygen to burn with.
tech.spacebreaker.hydrogen_engines.desc: Liquid hydrogen gives the highest chemical specific impulse, if you can keep it cold.
tech.spacebreaker.ice_shell_tectonics.de: Ariel's crust was pulled apart until long strips dropped between parallel faults, then icy lava flooded their floors: read the faults and you know where the warm ice once rose.
tech.spacebreaker.icy_moons.desc: Drill through kilometres of ice to the hidden oceans of Europa and Enceladus.
tech.spacebreaker.interplanetary_transfe: Hohmann transfers and launch windows: when to leave, and how much Δv it costs.
tech.spacebreaker.ion_propulsion.desc: A whisper of thrust for months on end: electric fields accelerate xenon ions to huge speeds.
tech.spacebreaker.isru.desc: Live off the land: oxygen from ilmenite, water from polar ice.
tech.spacebreaker.kuiper_belt_navigation: Forty times farther from the Sun than Earth, light takes five hours to reach home: navigate on your own, by the stars and by Pluto hanging still over Charon.
tech.spacebreaker.landing_systems.desc: Heat shields, parachutes and landing legs: getting down is as hard as getting up.
Pad, flame trench and service tower: a safe place to light a rocket.
tech.spacebreaker.liquid_fuel_engines.de: Pump RP-1 and liquid oxygen into a combustion chamber for throttleable, restartable thrust.
tech.spacebreaker.lunar_surveying.desc: Map the maria and highlands; find ilmenite, ice and the safest landing sites.
tech.spacebreaker.magnetospheric_physics: Ganymede is the only moon with its own magnetic field, a bubble inside Jupiter's: map it, and you can shelter inside it and read the ocean below by its echo.
tech.spacebreaker.martian_geology.desc: Ancient riverbeds, hematite spherules and perchlorate soils tell the story of Mars.
tech.spacebreaker.metal_pressing.desc: Roll ingots into thin, stiff plates for tanks, panels and hulls.
tech.spacebreaker.metallurgy.desc: Electric arc furnaces melt metals together: steel for towers, aluminium-lithium for tanks, superalloys for engines.
tech.spacebreaker.methane_engines.desc: Clean-burning methalox engines, fuelled by propellant made on Mars itself.
tech.spacebreaker.microgravity_mining.de: On a world where a hard swing throws you off the ground, drills need anchors: harpoons, screw piles and counter-rotating cutters that push nothing away.
tech.spacebreaker.nitrogen_glaciology.de: At -230 °C nitrogen is a soft rock: it flows in glaciers, turns over in slow cells a few blocks deep and floats mountains of water ice. Read it and you can build on it.
tech.spacebreaker.nuclear_fission.desc: Radioisotope generators and compact reactors where sunlight is too weak.
tech.spacebreaker.nuclear_thermal_propul: A reactor heats hydrogen directly: twice the efficiency of any chemical engine.
tech.spacebreaker.observational_astronom: Lenses, mirrors and patience: chart the sky before you try to reach it.
tech.spacebreaker.orbital_mechanics.desc: Orbit is falling and missing the ground: about 7.8 km/s sideways at low altitude.
tech.spacebreaker.orbital_shipyard.desc: Assemble ships too big to ever lift off a planet.
tech.spacebreaker.oxygen_distribution.de: Fill sealed rooms with breathable air and keep it there.
tech.spacebreaker.oxygen_storage.desc: High-pressure aluminium tanks and a filling station: five minutes of air per tank.
tech.spacebreaker.phobos_survey.desc: A captured asteroid or a chip of Mars? Grooved, dusty and so small you could jump off it.
tech.spacebreaker.plume_sampling.desc: Fly through the geysers of Enceladus and catch grains of its ocean: salt, silica and organic molecules, sampled without drilling a metre.
tech.spacebreaker.polar_ice_mining.desc: Heated drills for the permanently shadowed craters, where ice has waited in the cold for billions of years.
tech.spacebreaker.precision_manufacturin: A powered fabricator for the parts a hammer cannot make: cells, insulation and shield plates.
tech.spacebreaker.pressure_suits.desc: A personal spacecraft: a sealed garment that keeps you at one third of an atmosphere.
tech.spacebreaker.pressurised_modules.de: Sealed aluminium hulls, windows and doors that hold an atmosphere.
tech.spacebreaker.radiation_hardened_ele: Shielded vaults, error-correcting memory and wide-gap chips that keep working inside Jupiter's radiation belts.
tech.spacebreaker.radiation_hardened_sui: Polyethylene and tungsten layers against the radiation belts of Jupiter.
tech.spacebreaker.radiation_shielding.de: Layers of water, polyethylene and lead against solar storms and cosmic rays.
tech.spacebreaker.radio_communication.de: Antennas and transmitters to talk to spacecraft beyond the horizon.
tech.spacebreaker.radioisotope_power.des: Plutonium-238 decay heat turned into power: steady electricity where the Sun is too weak.
tech.spacebreaker.regolith_sintering.des: Bake lunar dust into hard bricks: radiation shielding you do not have to launch.
tech.spacebreaker.rovers.desc: Electric vehicles with wire-mesh wheels for driving across dusty plains.
tech.spacebreaker.sabatier_process.desc: Carbon dioxide plus hydrogen over a nickel catalyst gives methane and water.
tech.spacebreaker.satellites.desc: Put eyes and relays in orbit: mapping, weather and communication satellites.
tech.spacebreaker.solar_power.desc: Silicon cells on a sun-tracking mount: free energy whenever the sky is clear.
tech.spacebreaker.solar_shielding.desc: Gold-film sunshades and white radiators: on Mercury the Sun is seven times brighter and the ground reaches 430 °C.
tech.spacebreaker.solid_rocket_motors.de: Cast propellant grains: simple, powerful, and impossible to switch off once lit.
tech.spacebreaker.space_probes.desc: Uncrewed explorers that fly ahead and send back pictures of worlds no one has seen.
tech.spacebreaker.space_stations.desc: Dock modules together in orbit: a home, a workshop and a fuel depot above the sky.
tech.spacebreaker.spectroscopy.desc: Split starlight into a rainbow and read what distant worlds are made of.
tech.spacebreaker.staging.desc: Drop empty tanks on the way up. The rocket equation rewards every kilogram left behind.
tech.spacebreaker.suit_mk2.desc: Dust-proof joints, a longer life-support pack and a smarter helmet display.
tech.spacebreaker.suit_mk3.desc: A hard-shell suit for the Jovian moons: shielded, heated and built for long walks.
tech.spacebreaker.suit_upgrades.desc: Upgrade modules fitted to suit pieces at a smithing table.
tech.spacebreaker.tectonic_mapping.desc: Titania's canyons run straight for hundreds of kilometres, the cracks of a moon that swelled as its insides froze: map them and you can read its whole history from the walls.
tech.spacebreaker.thermal_regulation.des: Water-cooled undergarments and reflective layers for +120 °C sun and −150 °C shade.
tech.spacebreaker.thermal_suits.desc: Reflective gold-foil layers and liquid cooling for Mercury's day and the surface of Venus.
tech.spacebreaker.titan_expedition.desc: Thick nitrogen air and lakes of liquid methane at −180 °C: the only other world with rain, rivers and seas.
tech.spacebreaker.vacuum_engines.desc: Long nozzles that expand exhaust fully in space for a much higher specific impulse.
tech.spacebreaker.vertical_exploration.d: Rope anchors in ice, slow controlled descents and the patience to fall for minutes: how to get down Miranda's great cliff and back up again.
tech.spacebreaker.volcanic_heat_shieldin: Reflective multilayer suits and ceramic boots for walking beside Io's lava lakes, where the ground goes from -140 °C to molten in a few steps.
tech.spacebreaker.water_recycling.desc: Recover more than nine litres of every ten: humidity, wash water and the rest.
tooltip.spacebreaker.airlock_door: Airtight when closed. Opens by hand or redstone
tooltip.spacebreaker.atmosphere_processo: Separates the main useful gas of the local air; needs open air above
tooltip.spacebreaker.chemical_reactor: One solid and two fluids in; e.g. sulfur + water + oxygen → sulfuric acid
tooltip.spacebreaker.electric_drill: Digs stone and soil fast while charged. Charge it in the Suit Maintenance Station
tooltip.spacebreaker.electrolyzer: Hydrogen leaves on the left, oxygen on the right (seen from the front)
tooltip.spacebreaker.emergency_beacon: Away from Earth: calls a capsule that brings you home
tooltip.spacebreaker.environment_sensor: Use to read pressure, air, temperature, radiation, gravity and ground
tooltip.spacebreaker.guide_book: Everything you need to know, illustrated
tooltip.spacebreaker.habitat_kit: Use in empty space: unfolds a sealed 7×5×7 room with an airlock, windows, docking port, bunk, a solar array and a battery bank
tooltip.spacebreaker.habitat_kit.air: Put an oxygen tank in the distributor to fill it with air
tooltip.spacebreaker.hologram.hint1: Use: choose a structure · use on a block: place the projection
tooltip.spacebreaker.hologram.hint2: Sneak + use: layers · sneak + wheel: turn · sneak + use on a block: remove
tooltip.spacebreaker.ice_core_sample: Ancient cold-trap ice in layers: water and frozen volatiles
tooltip.spacebreaker.ice_melter: Ice to clean water; dry ice to carbon dioxide
tooltip.spacebreaker.mmu.hint: Fit onto an EVA torso; fly with jump and sneak
tooltip.spacebreaker.module.hint: Smithing table: Suit Upgrade Template + suit piece + module
tooltip.spacebreaker.oxygen.hint: Use while wearing an EVA torso to slot it in
tooltip.spacebreaker.oxygen_distributor: Pressurises the sealed room around it from a tank or piped oxygen
tooltip.spacebreaker.oxygen_filler: Refills tanks from a planet's breathable air, or from piped oxygen / liquid oxygen. Needs FE
tooltip.spacebreaker.part.capsule: Crew section: sits on the heat shield
tooltip.spacebreaker.part.cargo: Uncrewed cargo: goes in the capsule slot; docks at the station or lands on the beacon and unloads into the nearest chests
tooltip.spacebreaker.part.cargo.route: Between a station and a base it shuttles by itself: chests take deliveries, barrels hold what goes out
tooltip.spacebreaker.part.decoupler: Drops the stage below when it runs dry
tooltip.spacebreaker.part.engine: One per stage, at the bottom
tooltip.spacebreaker.part.fins: Radial: less steering loss on ascent
tooltip.spacebreaker.part.grid_fins: Radial: steering for the first stage
tooltip.spacebreaker.part.heat_shield.1: Heat shield: rated for reentry from low orbit
tooltip.spacebreaker.part.heat_shield.2: Heat shield: rated for reentry from the Moon
tooltip.spacebreaker.part.interstage: Drops the stage below; shields the engine above
tooltip.spacebreaker.part.isp: Isp: %s s sea level / %s s vacuum
tooltip.spacebreaker.part.landing_legs: Radial: needed to land on the Moon
tooltip.spacebreaker.part.parachute: Mount on top of the capsule for a soft landing
tooltip.spacebreaker.part.probe: Uncrewed probe: goes in the capsule slot; launch it from the console
tooltip.spacebreaker.part.propellant_hyd: In a hydrolox stage: LH2 %s mB, LOX %s mB
tooltip.spacebreaker.part.propellant_met: In a methalox stage: CH4 %s mB, LOX %s mB
tooltip.spacebreaker.part.satellite: Uncrewed satellite: goes in the capsule slot; launch it from the console
tooltip.spacebreaker.part.tank: Holds RP-1 kerosene and liquid oxygen
tooltip.spacebreaker.pipe: Carries up to %s mB/t. Sneak-use an end: pull from a block or an endless water source; with a filled container: let only that fluid through
tooltip.spacebreaker.power_monitor: Place against a battery bank: charge, net flow and time to full or empty
tooltip.spacebreaker.press_die: Used in the Press; not consumed
tooltip.spacebreaker.propellant_cartridg: Use on a rocket to fill every tank
tooltip.spacebreaker.regolith_excavator: Digs a 5x5 patch below, 16 deep, and feeds the machines beside it
tooltip.spacebreaker.regolith_heater: Molten regolith electrolysis: oxygen from rock
tooltip.spacebreaker.research_lab: Analyses tech disks and samples. Needs FE power.
tooltip.spacebreaker.rocket.hint: Use on the flame trench of a launch pad
tooltip.spacebreaker.rover: Two seats, battery-electric. Sneak-use: cargo. Use with a solar panel, an RTG or a pellet to fit it
tooltip.spacebreaker.rover.charge: Charges when parked next to a battery bank or cable
tooltip.spacebreaker.rtg: Up to %s FE/t, day and night, anywhere. Shielded casing
tooltip.spacebreaker.rtg_fuel_pellet.rad: Radioactive: a small dose while carried
tooltip.spacebreaker.safety_tether: A %s-block line from your belt to a block: you cannot drift away
tooltip.spacebreaker.safety_tether.hint: Use on a block to clip on, use again to unclip
tooltip.spacebreaker.sample.hint: Analyse in a Research Lab: may reveal a technology
tooltip.spacebreaker.sample_kit: Use on natural ground to take a field sample
tooltip.spacebreaker.sintering_furnace: Fuses regolith into building blocks with electric heat, no air needed
tooltip.spacebreaker.solar_panel: Follows the sun. Peak output: %s FE/t
tooltip.spacebreaker.solar_panel.here: Sunlight here: %s%% of Earth's (noon peak %s FE/t)
tooltip.spacebreaker.station_kit: Use in empty space: unfolds a 5×5 hull floor in front of you
tooltip.spacebreaker.suit.set: Sealed only with all four pieces worn
tooltip.spacebreaker.suit.tank_hint: Right-click with a tank or unit to fit it; with an empty cursor to take one out
tooltip.spacebreaker.suit_station: Stand on or beside it in a suit: tops up tanks and the Maneuvering Unit, slowly mends wear. Needs FE
tooltip.spacebreaker.sun_visor.hint: Sneak + use to toggle the sun visor
tooltip.spacebreaker.tank.cryogenic: Holds %s mB of a cryogenic liquid
tooltip.spacebreaker.tech_disk.hint: Analyse in a Research Lab to learn it
upgrade.spacebreaker.extra_oxygen.desc: Torso only: a third tank slot in the backpack
upgrade.spacebreaker.jetpack_booster.des: Torso only: stronger Maneuvering Unit thrust for the same gas
upgrade.spacebreaker.radiation_shield.de: Cuts the radiation dose by a quarter (stacks)
upgrade.spacebreaker.thermal_regulator.d: Widens the suit's rated range by 15 °C each way (stacks)
